title: Route events to the handlers that subscribed to their type

blocks.text: The billing service delivers its internal events through `EventBus`. Handlers subscribe to a type: the audit log to `Auditable`, the dunning job to `InvoiceEvent`, a debug tap to `Object`. Since the last refactoring the audit log stays empty, and the startup check warns that nobody handles `InvoicePaid`, although the dunning job does.
`publish` and `unhandled` already loop over the subscriptions. Finish the two `TODO`s in `src/main/java/practice/EventBus.java`:

items: `accepts(type, event)`: whether a handler subscribed to `type` receives this event;
`handles(type, eventClass)`: the same answer for a class, before any event exists.

blocks.text: A message the decoder can't map is published as `null`; it must reach no handler and must not throw. Two lines in total.

cases.says: an event reaches a handler subscribed to the event's own class
an event of an unrelated class reaches no handler
the startup check reports a class nobody subscribed to and not one with its own handler
a handler subscribed to a parent class receives events of its subclasses
publishing null reaches no handler, even one subscribed to Object, and doesn't throw
the startup check counts a handler subscribed to an interface as handling every class that implements it
the startup check counts a handler subscribed to a parent class as handling its subclasses

origin.section: instanceof Asks About the Object's Class at Run Time, and null Has None

concepts: instanceof is false for null, whatever the type, because null refers to no object.
instanceof tests the class of the object at run time, and is true for that class's superclasses and interfaces; Class.isInstance is the same test with the type as a value.
